summary: A twenty-two minute call in three parts. It opens on small talk about hair, Michigan and Michael's move to Florianopolis, then turns into a candid exchange about Michael's finances and a debrief on the Xiao Xie call from the previous day, which he self-critiques as talking far too much. The middle section is Chris and Angelo walking Michael through the CRM dialler — how to stop a lead who said he was not interested from recirculating into tomorrow's list — and Chris dictating a cold-call opener line by line for Michael to use on old no-show leads. It closes with Chris and Angelo discussing whether the SalesKick automated lead agent is worth keeping and a booking bug that is losing DM-set appointments.
notable: A COMMISSION-ONLY CLOSER DISCLOSED HAVING NOTHING IN THE BANK WHILE TAKING LIVE SALES CALLS — 'I'm looking at my bank account right now, and I'm stressed', 'this, I think is the legit, the tightest I've ever been financially where I'm like, what the ?' and, plainly, 'I got $0 in my bank.' The response was mindset coaching: 'the only thing that's going to knock you off is yourself. So just continue to keep grounding yourself every single day.' In the same week this rep improvised a $100 holding deposit, a $1,200 trial and an unspecified instalment plan on live calls.

THE SALESKICK AUTOMATED LEAD AGENT IS KNOWN TO BE DAMAGING LEADS AND IS STILL RUNNING — Angelo: 'I know a team that was using it, and they actually shut it off, because they were like, this is burning more people than it's helping.' Chris: 'Yeah, I've had a couple people say that', and 'there are moments where I watch it, and I'm like, this is pretty good. And then there's moments where I'm like, what happened here? What is even going on?' The stated plan is to keep sending feedback to the vendor rather than to pause it. This is the same agent — 'Sophia' — that the 07/06 meeting said had gone rogue and probably upset prospects.

CRM LEAD STATUS IS MANUAL AND LEADS RECIRCULATE IF NOBODY CLEARS THEM — Michael on a lead he had just dialled: 'This guy answered and he's like, I answered and he's basically like, wow, not interested. So, how do I, because what I understand is it'll take him off of this list, but he's going to pop up again tomorrow.' Angelo's fix is a manual status change: 'just put it in lost.' Separately, a prospect who cancelled a booked call sits in the no-show list — 'Why would he be in the no-show list if you mark him? Well, technically he canceled the sales call. That's why he's in there.' Cancellations and no-shows are therefore not distinguished in the list the team works from.

PROSPECT CALLS ARE BEING PUT THROUGH AI ANALYSIS — Chris on Michael's call from the previous day: 'I didn't look through the discovery, but based off. What I saw in the summary, I had an AI analysis of it, and I listened to the end.' A management judgement about a rep's call was formed partly from a machine summary rather than the recording.

A CLOSER WITH NO SETTING EXPERIENCE WAS PUT ON THE DIALLER AND GIVEN A SCRIPT DICTATED LIVE — 'I've never said before in my life'. Chris dictates it: 'hey, is this Lowe's? Yeah. Hey, what's up, man? This is just Michael here with Trevor's team. Um, the, you know, Trevor, the kettlebell guy. Does that ring a bell?' then 'it looks like you submitted an application and maybe booked a call, but it doesn't seem like maybe that happened. And I just wanted to call and make sure that you got everything you needed and see if maybe I could help. You got a minute?' The identification is honest — own name, Trevor's team — which is worth recording given the pilot's interest in how setters identify themselves. Michael asks whether to say the call never happened and is told 'You could. There's no right or wrong. Like, it's just a hook enough for them to kind of jog their memory.'

THE 07/09 XIAO XIE CALL IS CONFIRMED AS NOT CLOSED AND SELF-CRITIQUED — Michael: 'the Roy got. I reviewed the call. like, man, I'm talking way too much on this call.' Chris frames it as a timing objection. Michael's own diagnosis: 'I could have done a better job, like, selling, not telling... I was doing a lot of telling, and I think I could have elicited things more', and he describes being blindsided at the commitment check — 'he's like, Well, actually, I don't know if I want to commit to this right now. was like, wait, what the ? Like, I was not expecting that at all. So that's where it was kind of, and then that's when I went into, like, emergency mode.'

THE MANAGER ENDORSED STAYING ON PAST THE HESITATION — 'I applaud you for staying on with him. Like, I probably would have done the same thing, to be honest with you. I wouldn't say to, like, not stay on with somebody like that and see if you can build a case.' On that call the close ran twenty-three minutes past an explicit request for time and through a disclosed hard stop.

COACHED TO WEIGH A PROSPECT'S DISCRETIONARY SPENDING AGAINST THEM — 'if you find out like, dude, you're spending $600 a week on partying and doing all this other stuff... you can maybe quickly find out like, dude, it's not that you don't have the money. It's that you're just spreading yourself so thin because you're not willing to get rid of comfort and luxuries.' The same passage contains the more temperate instruction to walk away when the constraint is real: 'if you're really all in on this app thing, like maybe it isn't the right time to do this right now, but you should at least do something like, let me send you over this YouTube videos.'

Operational bug losing appointments: DM-set bookings time out. Angelo: 'if you go on the calendar and you submit and you're waiting and you're on the page to book a time, like, if you don't do it, it's going to refresh and then ultimately kind of time out and you're not going to be able to book a call.' The workaround proposed is for the DM setter to message the manager for open slots and book manually.
Angelo's assessment of the CRM: strong on application rebuilding, AI application grading and coaching feedback; weak on the automated lead agent and on the absence of a bookable calendar for setters.
Michael is paying $850 a month for a house in Florianopolis against $2,200 for a studio in Colombia, and says a stem cell treatment that did not work out is behind his current cash position.
